title: 2016 AMC 12B Problem 25
statement: The sequence \((a_n)\) is defined recursively by \(a_0=1,\) \(a_1=\sqrt[19]{2},\) and \(a_n=a_{n-1}a_{n-2}^2\) for \(n\ge2.\) What is the smallest positive integer \(k\) such that the product \(a_1a_2\cdots a_k\) is an integer?

solutions.text:
Write \(a_n=2^{\frac{b_n}{19}}.\) The recursion becomes \(b_0=0,\) \(b_1=1,\) \(b_n=b_{n-1}+2b_{n-2},\) solved by \(b_n=\tfrac13\bigl(2^n-(-1)^n\bigr).\) The product \(a_1\cdots a_k\) is an integer exactly when \(b_1+\cdots+b_k\) is divisible by \(19.\) Summing the formula for \(b_n\) gives \(b_1+\cdots+b_k=\dfrac{2^{k+1}-1}{3}\) when \(k\) is odd, and \(b_1+\cdots+b_k=\dfrac{2^{k+1}-2}{3}\) when \(k\) is even.

The order of \(2\) modulo \(19\) is \(18\) because \(2^9\equiv-1\pmod{19}\) and \(2^6\not\equiv1\pmod{19}.\) For odd \(k,\) divisibility therefore requires \(k+1\) to be divisible by \(18,\) first occurring at \(k=17.\) For even \(k,\) it requires \(k\) to be divisible by \(18,\) first occurring at \(k=18.\) Hence the smallest positive \(k\) is \(17.\)

Thus, the correct answer is A.
hints: The product is an integer exactly when \(b_1+b_2+\cdots+b_k\) is divisible by \(19;\) solve \(b_n=\tfrac13(2^n-(-1)^n)\) and use the order of \(2\) modulo \(19\)
